title: Context-aware log scrubbing and field-level encryption scheduler
creator: Asha Raman
description: Goal: Reduce PII exposure in observability streams while preserving signal for latency/error dashboards and tracing. Deliver a context-aware ingestion pipeline that: (1) detects high-confidence PII fields across logs and trace attributes using a lightweight rules + ML model ensemble, (2) supports configurable actions per-field (redact, pseudonymize, encrypt-at-rest, keep) per-tenant and per-route, (3) provides field-level encryption with key access logged to the audit stream, and (4) includes a retention scheduler that enforces differing retention windows and V1->V2 migrations without downtime. Must integrate with tracing hooks so spans can mark transient sensitive attributes (e.g., end-user identifiers) for immediate scrub or ephemeral caching only, and with metrics/log pipelines so cardinality reduction and anonymization preserves aggregations used by dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: PII detection runs at ingestion with <5% false positive rate on standard test corpus and adjustable thresholds per-tenant
Configurable actions (redact/pseudonymize/encrypt) available for each detected field via Console and infra config
Field-level encryption implemented for 'encrypt' action using customer/root KMS keys; every KMS decrypt request emits an audit event with actor and purpose
Retention scheduler enforces per-tenant retention windows and supports swift expiry with no observable impact on query latency for last-90-day data
Tracing hooks allow spans to opt-in/out of sensitive capture and are validated end-to-end in staging with sample traces
RBAC controls limiting decryption and raw-log access are enforceable and tested via integration tests and manual review
E2E performance impact on ingestion path <= 10% p95 increase for typical traffic profile; batch-aware optimizations documented
Documentation and runbook published: Confluence doc, upgrade/rollback steps, incident playbook, and a follow-up QA checklist
